english: It makes all the senses and their guṇa (here, their objects) shine forth, that is, it makes them known, or itself perceives them; it is devoid of all senses, unattached yet bearing all, nirguṇa (without the guṇa) and yet the bhoktṛ (enjoyer) of the guṇa. The verse does not teach Brahman by stripping away every attribute: making-known, bearing all, enjoying the guṇa, and the hands and feet everywhere of the verse before are attributes it is here said to have. What 'devoid of senses', 'nirguṇa' and the like mean was explained earlier, in the second chapter.
divergence_note: Read with Jayatīrtha's Prameyadīpikā on Madhva's bhāṣya (their 13.15): Madhva gives two sentences: sarvendriya-guṇābhāsa is read causatively, 'that which makes all the senses and the guṇa (qualities) shine', and the sense of 'devoid of senses' and the rest has been given earlier. Jayatīrtha places this in an argument. An opponent objects that here Brahman is meant to be made known only by denying every viśeṣa (particular attribute), so ascribing śakti (power) to it, as Madhva did on the preceding verses, is contradictory; Jayatīrtha answers that this very verse shows Brahman as having attributes, and cites 'hands and feet everywhere' (13.13), sarva-bhṛt (bearing all) and guṇa-bhoktṛ (enjoyer of the guṇa) as further instances. He also glosses guṇa as the objects of the senses, gives two senses of ābhāsa (makes them known, or perceives them), adds a grammatical note on the derivation from the root bhās, and identifies 'earlier' as the second chapter. That earlier explanation is not in the supplied text, so how Dvaita reconciles 'devoid of senses' and 'nirguṇa' with the attributes is not rendered here. Against Advaita and Advaita-bhakti, for whom the attributes only seem to belong to Brahman through adjuncts or māyā (illusory power) and the negations state the truth, and Śuddhādvaita, which makes Brahman the seat of contradictory attributes, the Dvaita reading treats the positive attributes as real and refuses to let the negations cancel them; the causative gloss is shared with the Bhakti rendering, which offers it as an alternative.
everyday_application: When a description of someone says both that they do something and that they lack something similar, do not let the negative cancel the positive; work out what the negative is actually excluding. A reference who says a candidate 'never micromanages' and also 'keeps every project on track' is not saying the candidate does not manage, so the useful question is which kind of managing is being denied and which kind is being claimed.
